rq3_entries.value: people explore the database, interpret how failures occur and matter, and decide how to use those insights for prevention (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "To enable the safe development and implementation of software, we advocate exploring our database to learn how software failures occur, what their impacts are, and how to prevent them." (p. 11)

rq3_entries.value: no — the database is designed for continued updating, not competence-contingent withdrawal (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "The FAIL database itself can then be kept up to date through periodic runs on new tranches of news data." (p. 11)

rq3_entries.value: users must continue interpreting and applying database insights; the paper specifies no reduction in that responsibility as expertise grows (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "This insight could inform policies around software: what are the ways in which people are affected by software failures? what policies, regulations, and standards could help prevent such failures?" (p. 11)

rq3_entries.value: single_session (0) — no user session was observed.

claim_entries.value: FAIL demonstrates automated analysis of news-reported software failures that prior work analyzed manually (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "Where prior work relied on manual analysis of such articles, FAIL demonstrates the novel capability of automated analysis." (p. 11)

claim_entries.value: working_system_evaluated — each pipeline component was validated against manually produced ground truth (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "To develop and validate each component, we developed a ground-truth dataset by manually performing each step of the pipeline." (p. 5)

claim_entries.value: prior manual analyses [96, 124] and Ko et al.’s semi-automated analysis [70] (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "Prior related work relies on manual analysis [96, 124] or semi-automation [70], whereas ours uses a fully automated approach." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: component tests measured article classification, incident clustering, fact extraction, analyst agreement, hallucination, and cost (PDF pp. 1, 6).
quotes: "FAIL achieved an F1 score of 90% for collecting news about software failures, a V-measure of 0.98 for merging articles reporting on the same incident, and extracted 90% of the facts about failures." (p. 1)
"The average proportion of incorrect facts introduced was 1%, with a maximum of 5%." (p. 6)
"The cost of running FAIL to gather incidents over the span of 12 years was $590, or $0.25 per incident." (p. 6)

claim_entries.value: open_source — code and a publicly viewable database are available (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "The code, prompts, manual analysis, and evaluation for FAIL, as well as a publicly viewable version of our database is available at: https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13761264." (p. 11)

claim_entries.value: the reported classification, clustering, extraction, hallucination, and cost results directly test the stated automated-analysis performance (PDF pp. 1, 6).
quotes: "FAIL achieved an F1 score of 90% for collecting news about software failures, a V-measure of 0.98 for merging articles reporting on the same incident, and extracted 90% of the facts about failures." (p. 1)
"FAIL’s accuracy appears to be acceptable to fully or substantially automate news failure analysis, depending on the application." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: software failure analysis from news reports — (PDF p. 2)
quotes: "We design and implement FAIL, an automated approach for large-scale analysis of software failures from news using LLMs." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the database supports present analysis and decisions about engineering, policy, and research (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "The resulting database can inform software engineering practice and research, policy making, and education." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: expert_or_professional — the stated users are researchers, engineers, and policymakers (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "The full FAIL database is available so that researchers, engineers, and policymakers can learn from a diversity of software failures." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: execution_or_skill_gap — experts can analyze failures manually but cannot feasibly execute the work at corpus scale (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "However, current approaches to obtaining open source intelligence (e.g., studying news articles reporting on failures) require costly expert manual analysis which limits the scale of analysis." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the study measures whether analysis can be automated accurately and cheaply (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "FAIL’s accuracy appears to be acceptable to fully or substantially automate news failure analysis, depending on the application." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — the applied pipeline produced a database of 2,457 incident records (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "Using FAIL we collected 2,457 incidents as reported in Table 6." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — reports separate open-ended postmortem content from reusable taxonomy fields (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "The failure report contains open-ended (postmortem) fields and multiple-choice (taxonomy) fields." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: distributed_support — the system combines complementary evidence from multiple articles for fuller incident understanding (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "The articles may have different information, e.g., based on different sources, so we want to analyze them together for a full understanding of the failure." (p. 4)

paper_code_entries.value: hybrid_or_multi_model — an LLM produces summaries and judgments while a separate sentence-transformer model supplies embeddings (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "For the approximation, FAIL prompts the LLM to create a summary of the failure as reported in each article, and then uses OpenAI’s sentence transformer (text-embedding-ada-002) to convert the summary into an embedding." (p. 4)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_era — the semantic analysis uses GPT-3.5 (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "We used a SoTA LLM publicly available at the time of writing (2024): OpenAI’s ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo-0125) [3]." (p. 6)

limitations: "This limitation of news articles makes it difficult to assess the non-software causes of an incident, even when done manually (40% inter-rater agreement for our manual analysts)." (PDF p. 6)
"We scoped our definition of news articles to mainstream media sources such as CNN and Wired, which may reduce the level of technical detail available." (PDF p. 11)
"This paper propagates the failure cause-effect relationships as indicated in the articles selected by FAIL." (PDF p. 11)
"In addition, FAIL relies on a Large Language Model (LLM) which may hallucinate and introduce incorrect cause-effect relationships." (PDF p. 11)

"Additionally, we acknowledge that our evaluation of FAIL was based on comparison to human analysts, and that the analysts may themselves have erred in their interpretation of the studied articles." (PDF p. 11)
"Any application of failure data drawn from the news media must acknowledge the potential biases of that media [84]." (PDF p. 11)
"A publication’s editors may sway which events are covered and with what frequency." (PDF p. 11)
"For example, the FAIL database is likely biased toward more large-scale, impactful, and “interesting” incidents." (PDF p. 11)
"The FAIL database is also likely geographically biased." (PDF p. 11)
boundary_conditions: "The resulting 11 news sources were: Wired, The New York Times, CNN, Daily Mail, The Guardian, BBC News, Fox News, The Washington Post, CNET, Reuters, and AP News." (PDF p. 4)
"We searched for news from these sources, matching these terms, from 2010 to 2022." (PDF p. 4)
"It does include articles from multiple languages, but as Ko et al. noted [70], failure coverage tends to focus on issues in the United States and Europe." (PDF p. 11)
